tasks.title: Session security

tasks.title: Dashboard embedding policy
tasks.detail: Serve an embed page that only frames allowlisted origins, with CSP frame-src derived from the registry, falling back to a deep link when embedding is not allowed.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover CSP header content and the fallback link.
tasks.note: dashboards.py serves GET /api/dashboards/{id}/embed as text/html with no-store. The page frames the recorded URL only when embed is true, enabled is true and the origin is on KUBERWEAVER_DASHBOARD_EMBED_ORIGINS; it then carries a per-record policy (default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-src <origin>; frame-ancestors 'self') and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, so only the portal origin can frame it. Otherwise the page has no iframe, sets frame-src 'none', names one of three reasons (embedding not requested, record disabled, origin not on the allowlist) and serves the deep link with target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer. Label and URL are HTML-escaped and the page loads no remote script, style or font. tasks.title: Durable environment state
tasks.detail: Add state per environment and stack, encrypted at rest, with generation and resource list, replacing per-job state as the source of truth.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover concurrent apply refusal, generation increment, and state surviving restart.
tasks.note: environment_state.py owns one record per (environment, stack) under a 32-hex identity derived from both names: generation (0 before the first apply), resources (address/type/name/mode, deduplicated and sorted), the committing job, the canonical-document digest and the encrypted document, plus a lease column. The document is a Fernet token encrypted with state.key (0600 in a 0700 directory under <state_dir>/environment-state); a missing key is never regenerated while documents exist, a replaced token or digest is reported as unavailable, and no HTTP route returns the document or creates/updates a record. An apply claims the pair exclusively, the claim row's primary key arbitrates across processes, the claim records the observed generation, and a commit requires the matching claim token and an unchanged generation; the commit writes the document, then the record, then drops the claim, and finally reads both back. Failures after the attempt marker keep the claim, so a stack whose apply may have mutated the host stays blocked; POST /api/environment-states/{id}/lease/release is the only way to clear it, is administrator-only, requires the job named by the lease and audits environment_state.lease_released. Every commit audits environment_state.applied. TofuExecutor uses the store when the kernel resolves it (provider.environments): it claims before apply, refuses a stack another job already committed, releases the claim only when no attempt marker was written, commits the two owned addresses, and on removal requires the record to name the same job and commits an emptied generation. A standalone executor keeps its per-job folder as its only record. PostgreSQL registers environment_state, environment_state_documents and environment_state_claim; the SQLite migration accepts the same tables. docs/ENVIRONMENT_STATE.md plus README, IMPLEMENTATION, OPENTOFU and CHANGELOG updates. 37 tests in tests/test_environment_state.py cover generation 1 then 2, encryption at rest and key modes, concurrent-claim refusal, stale expected generation, a lost claim, the generation CAS, restart survival, missing-key refusal, tampered token and digest, invalid scope/job/resource/document specifications, API reads without the document, 404, anonymous/viewer/operator refusals, CSRF, admin lease release with audit, agent read:infrastructure versus read:jobs, and the PostgreSQL tables; 4 tests in tests/test_tofu_execution.py cover the committed generation, an apply refused by a held claim, a stack already committed by another job, and removal committing an empty generation. Suite 1572 passed, 2 skipped; secret scan and diff check clean. Frontend not touched (API-only iteration), so tsc/build were not rerun.

tasks.title: Import existing resources
tasks.detail: Adopt an existing VM into state by UUID and ownership marker without recreating it.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover adoption, refusal when the marker mismatches, and idempotent re-import.
tasks.note: adoption.py owns the only path that turns an existing VM into state. POST /api/environment-states/adoptions takes environment, stack, connection_id, UUID and the kuberweaver-job:<32 hex> marker; it is administrator-only, needs the session CSRF token and is unmapped for agent tokens. It reads the VM once through the recorded connection (connection_inspector -> connections.access -> driver.read_resource) and never creates, reconfigures, powers on, stops or deletes anything. The ESXi extension now reports ownership_sha256, the SHA-256 of an annotation that starts with kuberweaver-job: and null otherwise, so the free-form annotation text never leaves the driver; a driver without that field fails closed. Refusals: 409 when the VM is missing or unreadable, the live UUID differs, the marker is absent or mismatched, the stack already has a committed generation, an apply holds the lease, or another stack recorded the UUID; 503 when no inspector is wired or the state key is missing; 422 for an invalid environment, stack, UUID, marker or connection. A first adoption writes generation 1 with source=adoption, job_id=null, one esxi_vm.<uuid> resource and an encrypted document (uuid, marker, name, power state, cpu, memory, connection, actor); every record now carries source/adopted and commit() resets them to apply/null. A repeat re-reads the VM, keeps the generation, rewrites nothing and audits environment_state.adoption_repeated, so a re-import cannot duplicate or advance; a changed annotation makes the repeat fail. environment_state_adoption(uuid PRIMARY KEY) is the ownership index, registered in the PostgreSQL DDL and the SQLite migration, and GET /api/environment-states/adoptions lists it for any signed-in role. docs/ENVIRONMENT_STATE.md amends the writer invariant (execution providers through the claim, plus this audited adoption path), and IMPLEMENTATION, V2_HYPERVISORS, README and CHANGELOG follow. 35 tests in tests/test_adoption.py cover adoption with its document/audit/index, uppercase UUID canonicalisation, marker mismatch, missing marker, absent ownership evidence, mismatched UUID, unreadable VM, inconsistent live rows, idempotent re-import with a second audit row, a changed annotation on re-import, second-stack refusal, applied-stack refusal, held lease, administrator/CSRF/agent refusals, 13 invalid bodies plus unknown and missing fields, restart survival, missing key, the connection-registry read shape, kernel wiring and PostgreSQL; tests/test_esxi_driver.py adds the ownership digest readback and keeps annotation text out of the inventory. Suite 1608 passed, 2 skipped. The deployed ESXi extension data/extensions/esxi-runtime/module.py was refreshed from examples/ after backing it up under data/extension-source-backups (untracked, never in Git), so the timer restart loads ownership_sha256; without that refresh adoption fails closed with 409.

tasks.title: Destroy with ownership proof
tasks.detail: Destroy action with annotation and UUID proof, quarantine window, cancellation, and rollback_failed semantics.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover refusal on foreign VM, quarantine cancel, and failed destroy state.
tasks.note: destruction.py owns the irreversible path. POST /api/environment-states/{id}/destroy takes connection_id, the VM UUID and the kuberweaver-job marker; it is administrator-only, needs the session CSRF token and is unmapped for agent tokens. It refuses unless the record has exactly one managed esxi_vm.<uuid> resource, no apply lease is held, and the live VM proves the UUID and annotation digest exactly as adoption does; for an adopted record the submitted marker must also equal the recorded one, so a re-annotation does not transfer ownership. The request writes environment_state_destroy (id PRIMARY KEY, registered in the PostgreSQL DDL and accepted by the SQLite migration) with status quarantined, a random destroy_id and not_before = requested_at + 15 minutes, and changes nothing on the host after the one proof read; a repeat with the same connection, UUID and marker returns changed=false with the original window, and a different VM is refused. While a destruction is quarantined or executing, an apply claim on the stack is refused. /destroy/cancel accepts only the current destroy_id and only while quarantined, writes cancelled and audits environment_state.destroy_cancelled; it can no longer succeed once execution has started. /destroy/execute is refused before not_before, after a cancel and on a second call, transitions atomically to executing, re-reads and re-proves the VM (the annotation can change during the window) and only then calls the driver's destroy_resource(connection, credentials, uuid, marker), which must return True only after confirming the VM is gone. Success writes generation+1 with resources [], source=destroy, job_id=null and destroyed {uuid, at, by}, then marks the destruction destroyed and audits environment_state.destroyed; the empty generation is written before the destruction row, so a failure in between is reported as unverified rather than success. A proof refusal or a driver without the method leaves failed with the stack unchanged and a new request allowed; a driver error, a non-True return or an unconfirmed state write leaves rollback_failed with requires_manual_review and audits environment_state.destroy_rollback_failed. /destroy/resolve closes only a rollback_failed record: intact re-reads the VM and requires the recorded UUID and marker, returns the record to failed with resolved_intact and allows a new request; destroyed records the administrator's observed evidence and commits the emptied generation with resolved_destroyed. The state record is never deleted, the adoption index keeps the UUID as a tombstone, and the bundled ESXi extension stays read-only, so execute answers 503 until a write-capable destroy_resource exists. docs/ENVIRONMENT_STATE.md gains the state machine, refusal table and resolution rules; IMPLEMENTATION, V2_HYPERVISORS, README and CHANGELOG follow. 38 tests in tests/test_destruction.py cover the quarantined record and audit, idempotent repeat, foreign-VM refusal before any host read, cross-stack refusal, changed and missing marker, unreadable VM, unknown state, held lease, apply refusal while quarantined, cancel and stale destroy_id, cancellation racing execution, early execute, the successful emptied generation with its encrypted document, re-proof at execution, unreadable VM at execution, rollback_failed on a driver error and on a failed state write, resolve intact with live verification, resolve destroyed, resolve refusals, multi-resource refusal, restart survival, administrator/CSRF/agent refusals, invalid bodies, the connection_destroyer confirmed-write contract and PostgreSQL. Suite 1646 passed, 2 skipped; secret scan and git diff --check clean. Frontend untouched.

tasks.title: Drift report
tasks.detail: Nightly read-only comparison of declared versus live resources, producing a diff report with no remediation.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover drift detection per field and the absence of any write call.
tasks.note: drift.py compares each durable state record with the hypervisor, field by field, and writes one report per record: the declared side is the encrypted document (adoption attributes at the top level, an applied document's resource values otherwise), the live side is one read_resource through the connection recorded for the stack. Compared fields are uuid, name, power_state, cpu and memory_mb; a field the document does not declare is not compared and does not appear in checked, so an absent attribute is never reported as null drift. Statuses are in_sync, drift (fields each carry declared and live), unverified (read failure, no inspector, no connection, or an apply lease or destruction in progress), unsupported (resource type or data source without a read-only reader), empty (no recorded resources) and unavailable (document cannot be decrypted); a read failure is never drift and absence is never inferred from a driver exception. POST /api/environment-states/drift/run is administrator-only with CSRF and audits environment_state.drift_checked with the counts; a concurrent run answers 409. The nightly DriftLoop runs every KUBERWEAVER_DRIFT_SECONDS (default 86400, 0 disables, 60..604800 accepted, an unusable value falls back and is reported in schedule.error) and writes no audit row; it starts outside testing only or when the interval is named explicitly. GET /api/environment-states/drift and GET /api/environment-states/{id}/drift answer any signed-in role and an agent token with read:infrastructure; the run route has no agent mapping. environment_state_drift is registered in the PostgreSQL DDL and accepted by the SQLite migration script; docs/DRIFT.md plus README, IMPLEMENTATION, ENVIRONMENT_STATE and CHANGELOG follow. 36 tests in tests/test_drift.py cover per-field drift for each of the four attributes, a foreign UUID, an unreadable resource, no reader, no connection, unsupported and data resource types, a lease, a quarantined destruction, generation 0, a missing key, an applied document that declares only its identity, both document shapes, restart survival, the absence of every write (the only driver call is read_resource, the state row and document bytes are unchanged, no claim or destruction row, one report row, and no audit row from the loop against one from the manual route), administrator and CSRF refusals, agent scope separation, unknown and unchecked states, interval parsing, loop repetition and failure isolation, kernel wiring and the PostgreSQL table; suite 1682 passed, 2 skipped; secret scan and git diff --check clean; frontend untouched.

tasks.acceptance: Tests cover digest mismatch refusal and pinned-revision execution.
tasks.note: declarations.py owns the only path that turns a committed CI bundle into an execution. A bundle at a pinned commit (a full 40- or 64-hex id, resolved with rev-parse and required to equal the submitted string) names one declaration file and one saved OpenTofu plan with SHA-256 digests; the request pins the revision, the bundle path and the bundle digest. Blobs are read with ls-tree -l and cat-file from the object database at that commit, never from the working tree: only mode 100644/100755 regular files are accepted, a symlink or submodule is refused, and paths use a conservative repository-relative grammar with no traversal, dot components, absolute paths or .lock suffixes. The bundle digest, both file digests, the ZIP plan magic and the declaration (schema_version, environment, stack, and a Graph whose name and environment must match) are checked before anything else; a mismatch is 409 and the applier is never called. POST /api/declarations/verify is administrator-only with CSRF and writes nothing; GET /api/declarations returns the repository status (disabled, configured or configuration_error, never the path), the applier status and one declaration_run row per stack, readable by any signed-in role; agent tokens have no mapping for either route. POST /api/declarations/execute re-verifies (a previous verify is never trusted), refuses 503 when no applier can run, takes the same environment_state claim an apply uses, refuses when the recorded generation differs from the bundle's base_generation or a lease or destruction is active, records status executing, hands the exact bytes to PlanApplier, commits generation+1 with the returned state and resources, audits declaration.executed and marks the run executed. A failure after the applier started keeps the claim and records failed with requires_manual_review and a fixed reason. PlanApplier stages the plan as <state_dir>/declarations/<run>/declaration.tfplan (0700 folder, 0600 O_EXCL and O_NOFOLLOW file), re-hashes it, runs only `tofu apply ... declaration.tfplan` (no init, no plan, no -out=, allowlisted environment including TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR, 600 s, capped output, 0600 artifacts, unexpected-artifact refusal) and reads the result with `tofu show -json`; provider text never leaves the process. Configuration is <state_dir>/config/declarations.json (schema_version 1, enabled, an absolute canonical local path to a worktree or a bare repository; no URL, no network, fail-closed on symlinks, duplicate keys and unknown fields). declaration_run is registered in the PostgreSQL DDL and accepted by the SQLite migration script. docs/DECLARATIONS.md plus README, IMPLEMENTATION, ENVIRONMENT_STATE and CHANGELOG updates. 66 tests in tests/test_declarations.py cover pinned verification with a working-tree edit and a newer commit, each of the three digest refusals, a plan edited under an existing bundle, unknown, short and symbolic revisions, a symlinked blob, six bad paths, invalid bundles and declarations including duplicate JSON keys, a non-plan artifact, base-generation, lease and human-administrator refusals, the configuration statuses, bare and worktree repositories, the PostgreSQL table, kernel wiring, the three routes with role, CSRF and agent checks, the real staging path behind an injected process boundary (apply argv, staged names, modes, unchanged bytes, no plan, init or -out=), a failed apply keeping the claim with a sanitized run row, and an unexpected-artifact refusal. Suite 1748 passed, 2 skipped; secret scan and git diff --check clean; frontend untouched.

tasks.title: Workload bricks in the portal
tasks.detail: Wire the workload executor into job preparation so a workload node can be planned, approved and executed from the UI, with evidence visible.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover the full path with a stub playbook and refusal for unpinned roles.
tasks.note: workload_execution.py adds WorkloadProvider under the manifest name ansible-workload-v1 with requires_saved_plan: prepare_plan validates the brick contract (pinned role version, roles.lock.json, lifecycle playbooks, assertions, data class), resolves target_uuid from the deployment evidence of a succeeded approved provisioning job in the same environment (uuid, guest_ip, poweredOn, name; one address or the preparation is refused as ambiguous, latest evidence pinned), re-reads the guest through the connection registry when one is wired, binds the managed SSH key by id and fingerprint and saves review.json 0600; the public plan carries plan_digest, actions, summary and bindings so the existing deployment view shows the fingerprint, actions and summary before approval, the approval digest pins the saved plan, execution re-checks the durable evidence, stages the private key into a 0600 file that is removed afterwards, runs snapshot, apply and verify through WorkloadExecutor with the kernel-guarded runner and returns sanitized evidence (assertions, changed count, address) while raw playbook output stays private; a failed apply or verify rolls back and a failed rollback becomes rollback_failed with manual review; manual rollback is refused because bricks have no recorded restore target. policy.py admits one-node workload graphs with no edges and no failure injection without the container target/port rules; plugins/web-nginx declares execution_provider ansible-workload-v1 and the two portal inputs target_uuid and ssh_key_id; configuration.py adds KUBERWEAVER_ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK with the venv default; docs/WORKLOADS.md plus README, CHANGELOG and the brick README. 9 tests in tests/test_workload_portal.py cover the full path with a stub playbook (prepared plan contract, approval, snapshot/apply/verify, assertions in the result, 0600 evidence, staged key removed, can_rollback false), the unpinned-role refusal, role-lock drift, missing target evidence, ambiguous evidence, a live identity change at preparation, a failed apply with rollback, workload scope and a mixed container node. Suite 1757 passed, 2 skipped; the tree secret scan and git diff --check are clean, while the history scan still matches the stub PEM line published in ed6e43c (see constraints); frontend untouched.

tasks.title: Zabbix preset
tasks.detail: Compose the PostgreSQL, Zabbix server, web and agent bricks as a preset graph on one VM.
tasks.acceptance: Preset validates, plan ordering respects dependencies, no new code path.
tasks.note: Four workload bricks are data: db-postgresql wraps geerlingguy.postgresql 4.3.0 and publishes a 0600 credential handoff for the generated database role; zabbix-server, zabbix-web and zabbix-agent wrap community.zabbix 4.2.0 collection roles, each with pinned requirements, a real roles.lock.json checksum, lifecycle playbooks, declared assertions and an honest data class (state for PostgreSQL, config for the other three). presets/zabbix-7.yaml declares the one-guest stack: database, server, web and agent, with server requiring database and web/agent requiring server. scripts/validate_preset.py loads the preset, refuses undeclared fields, portal inputs stored in the file, duplicate/unknown/dependent-later/cyclic steps, a bad UUID or key, a missing or drifted role lock and any step config that violates its brick; it then builds one complete one-node graph per step and proves each through the same Catalog and Admission the portal uses, printing the dependency order and the graphs. No runtime code path was added: the workload contract stays one brick per job, so the preset is submitted as four normal jobs in the printed order. Collection installs stay under the existing gitignore alongside roles. docs/PRESETS.md plus README, CHANGELOG, WORKLOADS and the bricks plan; 13 tests in tests/test_zabbix_preset.py cover the order, per-step admission, all four brick contracts, bad inputs and every refusal; backend suite 1770 passed, 2 skipped; secret scan and git diff --check clean; frontend untouched.
